title: Spaghetti alla Carbonara Classic

seo.metaDescription: Master the art of authentic Spaghetti Carbonara with our classic Italian recipe. Learn how to make this creamy, rich pasta dish with simple steps. Perfect for dinner!

seo.imageAlt: A steaming plate of classic spaghetti carbonara with crispy guanciale, egg yolk, and freshly grated Pecorino Romano cheese.

description: Spaghetti alla Carbonara is a quintessential Roman pasta dish, celebrated for its rich, creamy texture achieved without using actual cream. This classic recipe perfectly balances crispy guanciale, pungent Pecorino Romano, fresh eggs, and black pepper, creating an unforgettable culinary experience. It is a true testament to simple ingredients transforming into a masterpiece of flavor and tradition.

instructions.title: Prepare Guanciale and Cheese
instructions.text: Dice the guanciale into small cubes or strips. Finely grate the Pecorino Romano cheese. In a medium bowl, whisk together the egg yolks and the whole egg. Add about two-thirds of the grated Pecorino Romano and a generous amount of freshly ground black pepper to the egg mixture. Whisk until well combined and set aside.

instructions.title: Cook the Guanciale
instructions.text: Place the diced guanciale in a large, cold skillet or frying pan over medium-low heat. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, until the guanciale is crispy and has rendered its fat. This usually takes about 8-10 minutes. Remove the crispy guanciale from the pan with a slotted spoon and set aside on a plate, leaving the rendered fat in the skillet. Turn off the heat under the skillet for now.

instructions.title: Cook the Spaghetti
instructions.text: Bring a large pot of heavily salted water to a rolling boil. Add the spaghetti and cook according to package directions until al dente. While the pasta cooks, reserve about 1 to 1.5 cups of the starchy pasta water before draining. This water is crucial for creating the creamy sauce.

instructions.title: Combine Pasta and Guanciale Fat
instructions.text: Once the spaghetti is al dente, drain it quickly, reserving the pasta water. Immediately transfer the hot, drained spaghetti directly into the skillet with the rendered guanciale fat. Toss the spaghetti vigorously with the fat for about 1 minute, ensuring every strand is coated. This helps season the pasta and cool the pan slightly.

instructions.title: Create the Carbonara Sauce
instructions.text: With the skillet off the heat, or on very low residual heat, quickly pour the egg and cheese mixture over the hot spaghetti. Immediately add a ladleful (about 1/4 cup) of the reserved hot pasta water. Toss and stir continuously and vigorously with tongs, lifting the pasta to coat it evenly. The heat from the pasta and the pasta water will cook the eggs gently, creating a smooth, creamy emulsion. Add more pasta water, a tablespoon at a time, if needed, to achieve a lusciously creamy, not soupy, sauce. The key is to keep tossing to prevent the eggs from scrambling.

instructions.title: Finish and Serve
instructions.text: Add most of the crispy guanciale back into the pasta, reserving a small amount for garnish. Continue to toss until the sauce is perfectly emulsified and coats the spaghetti beautifully. Taste and adjust seasoning with extra Pecorino Romano and black pepper if desired. Serve immediately in warm bowls, garnished with the remaining crispy guanciale and an extra sprinkle of Pecorino Romano and freshly ground black pepper.

tips: Always use guanciale for authentic Carbonara; pancetta is a decent substitute but lacks the unique flavor and fat rendering properties of guanciale. Pecorino Romano is also non-negotiable for its sharp, salty taste.

The secret to a creamy Carbonara is the perfect emulsification of egg, cheese, guanciale fat, and starchy pasta water. Ensure your pan is off the direct heat when adding the egg mixture to prevent scrambling. The residual heat of the pasta is enough.

Serve Carbonara immediately. This dish does not hold well, as the sauce can thicken too much or separate. Garnish with extra black pepper and Pecorino Romano right before serving for the best experience.
